nahhas-irab:47-47.t: They knew that He would not place them with them, so this is by way of self-abasement, just as the people of Paradise say: رَبَّنا أَتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا ["Our Lord, perfect for us our light"; al-Taḥrīm: 8], and they say «الحمد لله» ("Praise be to Allah") by way of gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and they find delight in that.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: That is, from among the people of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: أَهؤُلاءِ is a pointing to the believing people whom you swore Allah would not reach with mercy; that is, you swore in this world that Allah would not reach them in the Hereafter with mercy. They rebuke them with that, and their grief was increased by its being said to them: ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ. ʿIkrima read دخلوا الجنة without the alif, with the dāl vowelled with fatḥa, and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read أدخلوا الجنة with kasra on the khāʾ, taking it as a past verb.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: أَنْ أَفِيضُوا عَلَيْنا مِنَ الْماءِ is like «أن تلكم الجنّة». The plural of تِلْقاءَ is تلاقيّ.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَهْواً وَلَعِباً is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), a naʿt (adjective) of «الكافرين»; it may also be nominative or accusative by an implied (muḍmar) word. كَما نَسُوا is in the position of the genitive by the kāf. وَما كانُوا بِآياتِنا يَجْحَدُونَ is conjoined to it, i.e. "and as they used to deny Our signs".

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: وَلَقَدْ جِئْناهُمْ بِكِتابٍ فَصَّلْناهُ: that is, We made it clear so that whoever reflects on it may know it; and it was said: فصّلناه means "We sent it down in separate parts". عَلى عِلْمٍ: "on Our part, of it". هُدىً وَرَحْمَةً: al-Farrāʾ said it is accusative by qaṭʿ ("severance"). Abū Isḥāq said: that is, "guiding, possessing mercy", so he made it a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «فصّلناه». Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: هُدىً وَرَحْمَةً in the genitive is also permissible. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is like وَهذا كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ مُبارَكٌ [al-Anʿām: 92]. Abū Isḥāq said: «هدى ورحمة» is also permissible [in the nominative] in the sense of "it is guidance and mercy".

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا تَأْوِيلَهُ is with hamza, because it is from آل يؤول; the people of Medina lighten the hamza and make it an alif. There are two views on its meaning: one of them is "do they await anything but what they were promised in the Qurʾān of punishment and reckoning", and the other view is "do they await anything but its tawīl", from looking toward the Day of Resurrection. يَوْمَ يَأْتِي is accusative by «يقول». فَهَلْ لَنا مِنْ شُفَعاءَ: «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنا is accusative because it is the answer to the interrogative. أَوْ نُرَدُّ: al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "or will we be returned?", and Abū Isḥāq said: it is conjoined to the sense, i.e. "will anyone intercede for us, or will we be returned?". Ibn Abī Isḥāq read أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ with both of them in the accusative, the meaning being "unless we are returned", as Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Ṭawīl] 148-
فقلت له لا تبك عينك إنّما ... نحاول ملكا أو نموت فنعذرا
(I said to him: let your eye not weep; we are only seeking a kingdom, or else we die and are excused.)
Al-Ḥasan read أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ with both of them in the nominative, and the reading agreed upon is أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ. قَدْ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: that is, they did not benefit from them, and whoever does not benefit from something has lost it.
وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ: what they used to worship of idols.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t:
إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ is the noun of «إنّ», (اللَّهُ) is its khabar (predicate). الَّذِي is a naʿt (adjective); and it is permissible in the Qurʾān [i.e. in such a structure] — إن ربّكم الله الذي — for «الذي» to be the khabar. خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ: had He, Mighty and Exalted, willed to create them in the shortest of times, He would have done so, but He knew that this was more fitting, so as to show His power to the angels one thing after another.
يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ: that is, He makes it like a covering for it; it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be resumptive; and likewise يَطْلُبُهُ. حَثِيثاً is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّراتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ: al-Akhfash said: they are conjoined to «السموات», i.e. "and He created the sun". It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir: وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّراتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: the Quranic words are printed with the standard accusative vocalisation although the reading described is in the nominative.]

nahhas-irab:56-56.t:
[Translator's note: the opening words of this entry appear garbled in the source; the ayah discussed is إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ.] The noun of «إنّ» and its khabar «فأما قريب», and He did not say «قريبا» [sic; i.e. «قريبة»]; there are six views on this. Among the best of them is that al-raḥma and al-ruḥm are one and the same, and it means pardon and forgiveness, as Ziyād al-Aʿjam said: [al-Kāmil] 149-
إنّ السّماحة والمروءة ضمّنا ... قبرا بمرو على الطّريق الواضح
(Generosity and manly virtue have been enclosed in a grave at Marw, on the clear road.)
The view of al-Farrāʾ is that قريبا came without the hāʾ only to distinguish between "near" in kinship and this; and one who argued for him said: such is the speech of the Arabs, as Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Ṭawīl] 150-
له الويل إن أمسى ولا أمّ هاشم ... قريب ولا بسباسة ابنة يشكرا
(Woe to him if he passes the evening with neither Umm Hāshim near, nor Basbāsa daughter of Yashkur.)
Abū Isḥāq said: this is a mistake, because the way of the masculine and the feminine is that they follow their verbs. The view of Abū ʿUbayda is that قريب is masculine on account of the masculinity of "place". ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: this is a mistake; had it been as he said, قريب would have been accusative in the Qurʾān, as you say: إنّ زيدا قريبا منك.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh permitted something like what Abū ʿUbayda said, as a remote possibility, as Labīd said:
[al-Kāmil] 151-
فغدت كلا الفرجين تحسب أنّه ... مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها
(She set off in the morning thinking that each of the two openings — behind her and in front of her — was the place of fear.)
These are three views. Al-Akhfash said: it may be made masculine just as some feminines are made masculine, and he recited: [al-Mutaqārib] 152-
فلا مزنة ودقت ودقها ... ولا أرض أبقل إبقالها
(No rain-cloud has poured down like its pouring, and no land has put forth herbage like its putting forth.)
He said: and it is possible that "mercy" here means rain. The sixth view is that this is by way of attribution (nasab), as one says: امرأة طالق ("a divorced woman") and حائض ("a menstruating woman"). [Translator's note: the source counts "six views" but the enumeration as printed is not fully explicit.]

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّياحَ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). الرياح is the plural of ريح for a larger number, and for a smaller number أرواح, because the yāʾ in ريح is changed from a wāw since a kasra precedes it and it is unvowelled. بُشْراً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ: there are six readings of it, and a seventh which is permissible. The people of the two Sanctuaries and Abū ʿAmr read نُشُراً with ḍamma on the nūn and the shīn; al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read نُشْراً with ḍamma on the nūn and the shīn unvowelled; al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read نَشْراً with fatḥa on the nūn and the shīn unvowelled; ʿĀṣim read بُشْراً with the bāʾ, the shīn unvowelled and with tanwīn, and it is related from him بُشْراً with fatḥa on the bāʾ. These are five readings. Muḥammad al-Yamānī read بشرى بين يدي رحمته on the pattern of حبلى, and the seventh reading is بشرا with ḍamma on the bāʾ and the shīn. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned their meanings in our book al-Maʿānī. It is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and whichever of them is a maṣdar (verbal noun) is like the saying «قتلته صبرا» ("I killed him in confinement"). حَتَّى إِذا أَقَلَّتْ سَحاباً: it [سحاب] is treated as masculine and feminine, and likewise every plural between which and its singular there is a hāʾ; and it may be described with a singular, so you say: سحاب ثقيل and ثقيلة. سُقْناهُ لِبَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ: «لبلد» and «إلى بلد» have one meaning. كَذلِكَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
وَالْبَلَدُ الطَّيِّبُ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). يَخْرُجُ نَباتُهُ is in the position of the khabar (predicate). ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read يخرج نباته بإذن ربه with ḍamma on the yāʾ. وَالْبَلَدُ الطَّيِّبُ is the one whose soil is good, and the one that is bad is the one in whose soil there are stones and in whose ground there are thorns; the one quick of understanding is likened to the good land. And the land that is bad, لا يَخْرُجُ إِلَّا نَكِداً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Ṭalḥa read إِلَّا نَكِداً [i.e. نَكْدا], dropping the kasra because of its heaviness; it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "possessing scantiness". Abū Jaʿfar read إِلَّا نَكِداً [i.e. نَكَدا]; this is a maṣdar in the sense of "possessing scantiness", as al-Khansāʾ said: [al-Basīṭ] 153-
فإنّما هي إقبال وإدبار
(For she is but coming and going.)

nahhas-irab:59-59.t:
لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ فَقالَ يا قَوْمِ: the fāʾ indicates that the second comes after the first. يا قَوْمِ is a vocative in construct (muḍāf); يا قومي is also permissible, on the original form. اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ: this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Jaʿfar read غيره in the genitive, and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. Abū ʿAmr said: I do not know the genitive or the accusative. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: the accusative and the genitive are both permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: the nominative is from two angles. One of them is that «غير» stands in the place of «إلّا», so you say ما لكم إله إلّا الله and ما لكم إله غير الله; on this view the genitive is not permissible, [just as] ما جاءني من أحد إلّا زيد is not permissible, because «من» only occurs in a negative (non-affirmative) context [lit. "is not in the affirmative"]. Sībawayh said: because «على» and «عن» are not treated thus — i.e. they are never redundant at all — then he said: nor «من» in the affirmative. The other angle of the nominative is that it is a naʿt (adjective) on the position, i.e. ما لكم إله غيره, and the genitive is on the wording. The accusative as exception is also permissible, but it is not frequent, except that al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative of «غير» in every place where «إلّا» would fit in its position, whether the sentence is complete or not, and they permitted ما جاءني غيرك. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is the dialect of some of Banū Asad and Quḍāʿa, and he recited: [al-Basīṭ] 154-
لم يمنع الشّرب منها غير أن هتفت ... حمامة في سحوق ذات أو قال
(Nothing kept her from drinking but that a dove cooed on a tall palm-tree laden with clusters.)
Al-Kisāʾī said: جاءني غيرك [in the accusative] is not permissible, because «إلّا» does not occur here. Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the Basrans the accusative of غير is not permissible when the sentence is not complete, and that is, in their view, among the ugliest of solecisms. Abū Isḥāq said: what led him astray — meaning al-Farrāʾ — was only the verse which Sībawayh recited with it in the accusative; غير is accusative in the verse only because it is annexed to something that has no inflection. As for ما جاءني غيرك [in the accusative], it is a solecism and an error.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t:
أُبَلِّغُكُمْ and أبلّغكم are one, as is said أكرمه and كرّمه, and as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 155-
ومن لا يكرم نفسه لا يكرم
(And whoever does not honour himself is not honoured.)
[Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; the intended pair is أُبْلِغُكُم / أُبَلِّغُكُم.]

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ: the wāw is vowelled with fatḥa because it is a conjunctive wāw upon which the interrogative alif has entered for affirmation (taqrīr). The way of the wāw is to enter upon the interrogative particles, except the alif, because of its strength.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: وَإِلى عادٍ: if you wish you may make it a diptote, it being a name of the tribe, as He, Mighty and Exalted, said: وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عاداً الْأُولى [al-Najm: 50]; and whoever declines it fully makes it a name of the clan (ḥayy). أَخاهُمْ is conjoined, and it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the implied structure is "And to ʿĀd We sent their brother". هُوداً is a badal (substitute); it is declined although it is foreign, because of its lightness, since it is of three letters; it may also be Arabic, derived from هاد يهود.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: لَيْسَ بِي سَفاهَةٌ: had it been ليست it would have been permissible; the masculine is because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and something separates it from the verb.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t:
خُلَفاءَ is the plural of خليفة treated as masculine according to the meaning, and خلائف [is its plural] according to the wording. وَزادَكُمْ فِي الْخَلْقِ بَصْطَةً: al-Farrāʾ said: it is related that the tallest of them was a hundred cubits and the shortest of them sixty cubits.
بَصْطَةً with ṣād is permissible because a ṭāʾ comes after it.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: قالَ قَدْ وَقَعَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ رِجْسٌ وَغَضَبٌ أَتُجادِلُونَنِي فِي أَسْماءٍ سَمَّيْتُمُوها أَنْتُمْ وَآباؤُكُمْ ما نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ بِها مِنْ سُلْطانٍ فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ (71) فِي أَسْماءٍ سَمَّيْتُمُوها: the second object is omitted, i.e. "you named them gods".

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: وَإِلى ثَمُودَ is a diptote because it is made a name of the tribe. Abū Ḥātim said: it is a diptote because it is foreign; this is an error, because it is derived from al-thamad (scanty water). Al-Farrāʾ read أَلا إِنَّ ثَمُودَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ [Hūd: 68] taking it as a name of the clan, and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read وَإِلى ثَمُودَ أَخاهُمْ صالِحاً fully declined.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: Al-Ḥasan read وَتَنْحِتُونَ الْجِبالَ with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ; it is a dialect form, and there is in it one of the guttural letters, so it came on the pattern faʿala yafʿalu. Al-Aʿmash read ولا تعثوا with kasra on the tāʾ, taking it from عثي يعثى, not from عثا يعثو.

nahhas-irab:80-81.t: وَلُوطاً is accusative because it is conjoined, i.e. "and We sent Lūṭ"; it may also be accusative in the sense of "and remember", and likewise what preceded of its like, except that al-Farrāʾ permitted «وإلى عاد أخوهم هود» [in the nominative] because it has something to make it nominative, while in his view this is not permissible for Lūṭ. Abū Isḥāq said: one of the grammarians — meaning al-Farrāʾ — claimed that لوط may be derived from لطت الحوض ("I plastered the cistern"). He said: this is a mistake, because foreign names are not derived. أَتَأْتُونَ الْفاحِشَةَ is an interrogative carrying the sense of affirmation (taqrīr). The readers differed over what follows it. Abū ʿAmr read it as an interrogative, except that he softened the hamza, making it between hamza and yāʾ; ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza also read it as an interrogative, but they pronounced the hamza fully, reading أانكم; al-Kisāʾī and Nāfiʿ read the second without hamza, and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He and al-Kisāʾī both argued from His saying, Mighty and Exalted: أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخالِدُونَ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 34], where He did not say أفهم, and from His saying: أَفَإِنْ ماتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ [Āl ʿImrān: 144], where He did not say أانقلبتم [the source prints: انقلبتم]. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is related of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he inclined to the view of Abū ʿUbayd and al-Kisāʾī, and this is among the ugliest of errors, because they likened two things to something they do not resemble: the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of a single thing, so there cannot be two interrogatives in them, like the mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); thus أفإن متّ أفهم الخالدون is not permissible, just as أزيد أمنطلق is not permissible. The story of Lūṭ ﷺ contains two sentences, so you may ask a question about each one of them, and omission from the second is permissible because the first indicates it; but the preferred choice is to lighten the second hamza, and this is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ is mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: وَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ: the khabar (predicate) is أَنْ قالُوا. If you make [جواب] accusative, then the noun [of كان] is «أن قالوا», i.e. "except their saying". [Translator's note: as printed, the first clause presupposes the nominative جوابُ; the Quranic text has the accusative جوابَ, which is what the second clause explains.]

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ is conjoined to the hāʾ. إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ is an exception from an affirmative statement.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t: وَإِلى مَدْيَنَ is a diptote because it is the name of a city; it was also said: because it is the name of a tribe, and it was said: because of foreignness; the soundest is the first. أَخاهُمْ is conjoined. فَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ is from أوفى; one also says وفى, and in that dialect [it would be] فأوفوا [i.e. فَفُوا]. [Translator's note: the dialect form is printed as فأوفوا in the source.]

nahhas-irab:86-86.t: Al-Akhfash said: وَلا تَقْعُدُوا بِكُلِّ صِراطٍ means "on every path"; "So-and-so is بالبصرة" and "في البصرة" are one. تُوعِدُونَ وَتَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ: i.e. from the road that leads to obedience to Allah, Mighty and Exalted. وَتَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً: two objects, the implied structure being "they seek for it crookedness". One says: in religion and in a matter there is عِوَج, and in a stick there is عَوَج.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: وَإِنْ كانَ طائِفَةٌ: masculine according to the meaning; according to the wording [it would be] كانت.

nahhas-irab:89-89.t: وَما يَكُونُ لَنا أَنْ نَعُودَ «فيها» is the noun of يكون. إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ is in the position of the accusative, and there are two construals of it. Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. "except by the will of Allah, Mighty and Exalted". He said: and this is the view of the people of the Sunna. The other construal is that it is an exception not of the same kind as the first, and there are two views on its meaning: one of them is "unless Allah wills to make us worship Him by something of what you follow", and the other view is that it is like حَتَّى يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِياطِ [al-Aʿrāf: 40]. [Translator's note: "«فيها» is the noun of يكون" is as printed; the noun of يكون is the interpreted maṣdar أن نعود.]

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read فكيف إيس على قوم كافرين; this is the dialect of Tamīm, who say: أنا اضرب [i.e. with kasra on the prefix of the imperfect]. [Translator's note: the reading is presumably إيسى, with kasra on the prefix; it is printed as إيس.]

nahhas-irab:97-98.t: أَفَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ الْقُرى is like أوعجبتم, and likewise أَوَأَمِنَ in this reading. Two forms are related from Nāfiʿ: Qālūn and most people related from him that he read أَوَأَمِنَ with the wāw unvowelled, and Warsh related from him أومن with the wāw vowelled and the hamza dropped. The two forms go back to one meaning, because he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the wāw when he wanted to lighten it and drop it. The meaning of «أو» here is passing from one thing to another, and its like is His saying, Mighty and Exalted: إِنْ يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ أَوْ إِنْ يَشَأْ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ [al-Isrāʾ: 54].

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: The people of the two Sanctuaries and Abū ʿAmr read أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْأَرْضَ with the yāʾ, so «أن» is in the position of the nominative on this reading. Mujāhid and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read with the nūn: أولم نهد. Abū ʿAmr said: the reading with the nūn is impossible. Abū Jaʿfar said: «أن» is in the position of the accusative on the reading of whoever read with the nūn, in the sense of "because We struck them for some of their sins", and the sentence is complete; then He, Mighty and Exalted, said: [وَنَطْبَعُ] عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ [لا يَسْمَعُونَ]. It [نطبع] cannot be conjoined to «أصبناهم», because أصبناهم is past and نطبع is future; al-Farrāʾ permitted the conjunction, because the future and the past occur here with one meaning.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ: al-Akhfash said: i.e. "it was not that they would be judged to have faith, given their denial", i.e. they are not believers given their denial. Others said: this concerns particular people. كَذلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِ الْكافِرِينَ: [the kāf] is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: وَما وَجَدْنا لِأَكْثَرِهِمْ مِنْ عَهْدٍ is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "We did not find for most of them a covenant"; «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. There are two views on it: one is that the meaning is "We did not find in most of them fidelity to the covenant", i.e. fidelity to a covenant — i.e. when a covenant was made with them they did not fulfil it. The second view is that «العهد» means obedience, because obedience is incumbent on a person just as fidelity to the covenant is incumbent on him. وَإِنْ وَجَدْنا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفاسِقِينَ: al-Farrāʾ says: the meaning is "We found most of them only defiantly disobedient", and Sībawayh holds that this «إن» is the heavy one, lightened, and the lām is then required.

nahhas-irab:105-105.t:
حَقِيقٌ عَلى أَنْ لا أَقُولَ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا: this is the reading of Nāfiʿ and Shayba [i.e. عَلَيَّ]. Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAmr, the people of Mecca and the people of Kufa read (على ألّا) lightened, in the sense of "worthy" and "apt"; one says: فلان خليق بأن يفعل, جدير أن يفعل, and على أن يفعل, with one meaning. The meaning of «حقيق عليّ» is "incumbent on me", and «أن» on this reading is in the position of the nominative. In the written text (al-sawād) it is joined in one place and separate in another place. The grammarians have discussed this. Al-Mulham, the companion of al-Akhfash Saʿīd ibn Masʿada, said: among the Arabs are those who assimilate with nasalisation (ghunna) and those who assimilate without nasalisation; whoever assimilates with nasalisation writes it separate, and whoever assimilates without nasalisation writes it joined, because he has removed the nūn and the nasalisation in it. Al-Qutabī said: whoever makes it govern the accusative writes it joined, and whoever does not make it govern the accusative writes it separate, as in أَفَلا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا [Ṭāhā: 89]; this is separate because there is an implied element (iḍmār) in it. Abū Jaʿfar said:
And I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: none of this may be written except separate, because it is «أن» upon which «لا» has entered.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t: فَأَلْقى عَصاهُ فَإِذا هِيَ: the wāw was dropped because it is unvowelled and the alif is unvowelled; فألقى عصا هو فإذا هي is also permissible, with the wāw [pronounced] — the hāʾ being between two unvowelled letters. [Translator's note: this sentence is somewhat garbled in the source; the point concerns the pronunciation of the pronoun -hu in عصاهُ.] فَإِذا هِيَ ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the meaning of مبين is that it is clearly a serpent, not confusing. This is the «إذا» of surprise; you say: خرجت فإذا عمرو جالس ("I went out, and there was ʿAmr sitting"), and the accusative is also permissible. Al-Kisāʾī said: because the meaning is "I came upon him suddenly". One of the Basrans said: had it been as he said, the noun would be accusative. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: I asked Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd how «إذا» came to be the khabar of a concrete noun, and he said: here it is an adverb of place. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: in my view it has the sense of occurrence.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ: accusative by «يريد». فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ: it may be that «قالوا» was [addressed] to Pharaoh alone — «فماذا تأمرون» — as tyrants are addressed; and it may be that «قالوا» was to him and his companions. «ما» is in the position of the nominative if «ذا» means «الذي», and in the position of the accusative if (ما) and (ذا) are one thing.

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: قالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخاهُ: this is the reading of the people of Medina, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī [i.e. أَرْجِهِ]; the rest of the people of Kufa read أَرْجِهْ وَأَخاهُ with the hāʾ unvowelled; and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read أرجئه وأخاه with an unvowelled hamza and the hāʾ with ḍamma. On the first reading there are three views: one is that it is by substitution for the hamza; and al-Kisāʾī said: Tamīm and Asad say أرجيت الأمر when you have postponed it; and the third view was stated by Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, who said: it is taken from رجا يرجو, i.e. "give him hope and let him hope"; the hāʾ has kasra by assimilation (itbāʿ), and ḍamma on it is permissible according to the original. Making it unvowelled is a solecism, permissible only in anomalous instances of poetry. The hamza is good and fine, were it not for contradicting the written text (al-sawād), except that it can be argued for on the ground that the like of this is dropped from the script. وَأَخاهُ is conjoined to the hāʾ. حاشِرِينَ is accusative by the verb.

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: يَأْتُوكَ is jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the imperative; therefore the nūn was dropped from it. The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read بكلّ سحّار عليم, and the rest of the people read ساحِرٍ, and so it is in the written text throughout; contradicting the written text must be avoided.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t: وَجاءَ السَّحَرَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ: mention of the sending for them is omitted because the hearer knows it.

nahhas-irab:115-115.t:
قالُوا يا مُوسى إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ: «أن» is in the position of the accusative according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, as he said: [al-Basīṭ] 156-
قالوا الرّكوب فقلنا تلك عادتنا
(They said: "Riding!" and we said: "That is our custom.")
Al-Farrāʾ said: there is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: Moses, upon him be peace, said to them: "You will never overcome your Lord nor nullify His signs." This is among the inimitable features of the Qurʾān, the like of which does not occur in people's speech nor are they capable of it: it brings a short wording that gathers much meaning. [Translator's note: the attribution of this last passage to this ayah is as printed; it appears to belong to the next ayah (116).]

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: وَجاؤُ بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ: i.e. great in their eyes, not great in reality.

nahhas-irab:117-117.t: It is related from ʿĀṣim: فَإِذا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ lightened [i.e. تَلْقَفُ]; and on this reading «تلقف» [i.e. تَلْقَفُ] is permissible because it is from لَقِفَ. ما يَأْفِكُونَ: i.e. what they falsify, because they brought ropes and put mercury in them so that they moved, and they said: these are snakes.

nahhas-irab:119-119.t: وَانْقَلَبُوا صاغِرِينَ: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Its verb is صغر يصغر, [maṣdars] صغرا, صغورا and صغارا.

nahhas-irab:126-126.t: Khārija said: al-Ḥasan read وَما تَنْقِمُ مِنَّا [i.e. تَنْقَمُ]. Al-Akhfash said: it is a dialect form.

nahhas-irab:127-127.t:
وَيَذَرَكَ وَآلِهَتَكَ: the answer to the interrogative. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is accusative on the ẓarf [i.e. ṣarf, "deflection"]. [Translator's note: as printed «الظرف»; al-Farrāʾ's term is presumably الصرف.] In the reading of Ubayy: أَتَذَرُ مُوسى وَقَوْمَهُ لِيُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وقد تركوا أن يعبدوك وَآلِهَتَكَ. قالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبْناءَهُمْ and سنقتّل, for multiplicity [i.e. the forms سَنَقْتُلُ / سَنُقَتِّلُ].
Abū Isḥāq said, from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh. [Translator's note: this line is incomplete in the source.]

nahhas-irab:130-130.t:
وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِالسِّنِينَ: he said: with hunger. Among the Arabs are those who inflect the nūn in السنين, and al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Wāfir] 157-
أرى مرّ السّنين أخذن منّي ... كما أخذ السّرار من الهلال
(I see the passing of the years has taken from me, as the last night of the month takes from the crescent.)
Sībawayh recited this verse with fatḥa on the nūn, but he recited in this [matter] something for which nothing else is permissible, namely his saying: [al-Wāfir] 158-
وقد جاوزت رأس الأربعين
(And I have passed the head of forty.)
Al-Farrāʾ related from Banū ʿĀmir that they say: أقمت عنده سنينا يا هذا ("I stayed with him for years, O you"), declined; he said: and Banū Tamīm do not decline it, and say: مضت له سنين يا هذا.

nahhas-irab:131-131.t:
وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ is a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). يَطَّيَّرُوا is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the original is يتطيّروا, and the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ. Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read تطيّروا, taking it as a past verb. The meaning of تطيّروا is "they took an evil omen"; the origin of this is from birds (al-ṭayr), then their use of it became frequent until it was said of everyone who took an evil omen: تطيّر.
Al-Ḥasan read ألا إنّما طيرهم عند الله, plural of طائر. وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ: i.e. they do not know that the drought and hardships that befell them were only from Allah, Mighty and Exalted, because of their sins, not from Moses ﷺ and his people.

nahhas-irab:132-132.t: وَقالُوا مَهْما: the Kufans related مهما with its meaning. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the original is «ما ما», the first being for the condition and the second the one which is added in your saying: أينما تجلس أجلس; they disliked combining two particles whose wording is the same, so they substituted a hāʾ for the alif and said مهما. Abū Isḥāq said: some said its origin is «مه», i.e. "stop". مَهْما تَأْتِنا بِهِ مِنْ آيَةٍ is a condition, and the apodosis is [after] لِتَسْحَرَنا بِها: فَما نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ.

nahhas-irab:133-133.t:
فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الطُّوفانَ: al-Akhfash said: plural of طوفانة. وَالْجَرادَ is the plural of جرادة for masculine and feminine; if you want to distinguish you say: رأيت جرادة ذكرا ("I saw a male locust"). وَالضَّفادِعَ is the plural of ضفدع. وَالدَّمَ is conjoined. Abū Isḥāq said: آياتٍ مُفَصَّلاتٍ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). He said:
And it is related that between one sign and the next there were eight days.

nahhas-irab:137-137.t:
وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغارِبَهَا: two objects. الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها is in the position of the accusative [as a naʿt] of مشارق and مغارب, and it may be genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «الأرض». Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ claimed that the original is "in the easts of the land and in its wests", then «في» was dropped and it became accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: and «أورثنا» falls on «التي»; and al-Farrāʾ [also] permitted them to be two objects, as was stated before. وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ is nominative by its verb. الْحُسْنى is its naʿt. It is related from ʿĀṣim: كلمات ربّك الحسنى.
وَما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ is an eloquent dialect form. Al-Kisāʾī said: Banū Tamīm say «يعرشون» [i.e. يَعْرُشُونَ], and ʿĀṣim read thus. One also says عكف يعكف and يعكف [i.e. يَعْكُفُ / يَعْكِفُ], and the maṣdar of all of them is on the pattern fuʿūl.

nahhas-irab:140-140.t: قالَ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِيكُمْ: two objects, one of them by means of a particle; the original is أبغي لكم. إِلهاً is accusative as specification (bayān). وَهُوَ is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is فَضَّلَكُمْ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ.

nahhas-irab:142-143.t:
وَواعَدْنا مُوسى ثَلاثِينَ لَيْلَةً: two objects, i.e. the completion of thirty nights. We have mentioned واعدنا and وعدنا in Sūrat al-Baqara. وَأَتْمَمْناها بِعَشْرٍ: the hāʾ was dropped because it is a number for a feminine. فَتَمَّ مِيقاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً: the benefit of this — when it is known that thirty and ten are forty — is that it would have been possible for the ten to be other than nights, so when He said "forty nights" it was known that they were nights. It was also said: it is emphasis. A third answer, the best of them: it would have been possible for the ten to be the completion of the thirty, so His saying فَتَمَّ مِيقاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً conveyed that the ten were besides the thirty. وَقالَ مُوسى لِأَخِيهِ هارُونَ اخْلُفْنِي فِي قَوْمِي: [هارون] as a badal (substitute); «هارون» [in the nominative] as a vocative is also permissible. It is from خلف يخلف, i.e. "be a successor for me". One says خلف الله عليه بخير when someone dies for whom no replacement is had, [such as] the two parents; and أخلف الله عليه when someone dies for whom a replacement is had, [such as] the two parents [sic], and أخلف الله عليه when someone dies for whom a replacement is had, [such as] brothers and those like them. [Translator's note: the passage appears corrupt; the repeated clause and "the two parents" in the second clause are as printed.] وَأَصْلِحْ has a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ), and likewise أَرِنِي.
As for أَنْظُرْ, it is the alif of the [first-person] self, so for that reason it is disjunctive; أنظر is jussive because it is an answer. فَإِنِ اسْتَقَرَّ مَكانَهُ is a condition, and the apodosis is فَسَوْفَ تَرانِي. فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّى رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا: this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Basra; its correctness is indicated by دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا [al-Fajr: 21], and by the fact that الجبل is masculine. The people of Kufa read جعله دكّاء, whose construal in Arabic is "He made it like a flattened (dakkāʾ) land"; the masculine is أدكّ, and the plural of دكّاء is دكّاوات and دكّ. وَخَرَّ مُوسى صَعِقاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَلَمَّا أَفاقَ قالَ سُبْحانَكَ: assimilation is permissible. سُبْحانَكَ is a maṣdar (verbal noun). تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ: one says تاب when one returns. Repentance is that one regrets what one has done, intends not to return to it, and desists from the act at once; these are three conditions of repentance. وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ is mubtadaʾ and khabar. Nāfiʿ read وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ with the alif retained in continuous reading; the better is to drop it in continuous reading, and retaining it is an anomalous dialect form outside analogy, because the alif was brought only to show the fatḥa, and when you read continuously it [the fatḥa] is not lost, so there is no point to the alif.

nahhas-irab:144-145.t: فَخُذْ ما آتَيْتُكَ: one does not say أوخذ, though it is the analogical form — just as one says أومر فلانا — because it was heard from the Arabs thus. It was said there is a reason for it: the khāʾ is one of the guttural letters, and likewise the hamza. As for أومر, it is said; and in accordance with this is His saying, Mighty and Exalted: وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُوا بِأَحْسَنِها. If you say مر فلانا, this is the more common, and أومر is permissible.

nahhas-irab:146-146.t:
وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Basra; the people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim read الرشد [i.e. الرَّشَد]. Abū ʿUbayd said: Abū ʿAmr distinguished between الرُّشد and الرَّشَد, saying: الرُّشد is in [worldly] soundness and الرَّشَد in religion. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh holds that الرُّشد and الرَّشَد are one, like السُّخط and السَّخَط, and al-Kisāʾī said likewise. Abū Jaʿfar said: what is sound from Abū ʿAmr is other than what Abū ʿUbayd said. Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq said: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from his father, from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: when al-rushd is in the middle of an ayah it is unvowelled, and when it is at the end of an ayah it is vowelled. Abū Jaʿfar said: by "the end of an ayah" Abū ʿAmr means something like وَهَيِّئْ لَنا مِنْ أَمْرِنا رَشَداً [al-Kahf: 10]; so in his view they are two dialect forms with one meaning, except that he vowelled this one with fatḥa so that the ayahs would agree. One says رشَد يرشُد and رشِد يرشَد, and Sībawayh related رشَد يرشَد [sic]. The reality of al-rushd and al-rashad in the language is that a person attains what he wants, and it is the opposite of disappointment; and the reality of al-ghayy in the language is disappointment. Allah, Mighty and Exalted, said: وَعَصى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوى [Ṭāhā: 121], and the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 159-
فمن يلق خيرا يحمد الناس أمره ... ومن يغولا يعدم على الغيّ لايما
(Whoever meets with good, people praise his affair; and whoever fails (yaghwi) will not lack someone to blame him for his failing.)

nahhas-irab:147-147.t: وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَلِقاءِ الْآخِرَةِ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ. هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ: the khabar of [the verb] whose agent is not named [i.e. the object of the passive verb].

nahhas-irab:148-148.t: وَاتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسى مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ: this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Basra; the people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim read مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ with kasra on the ḥāʾ [i.e. حِلِيِّهِم]; and Yaʿqūb read مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and lightened [i.e. حَلْيِهِم]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the plural of حَلْي is حُلِيّ and حِلِيّ, like ثَدْي and ثُدِيّ; the original is حُلُويّ, then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, so the lām took kasra because of its adjacency to the yāʾ, and the ḥāʾ takes kasra because of the kasra of the lām, and ḍamma according to the original. As for عِصِيّ, its original is عُصُوّ, because it is from the wāw-roots; then it underwent weakening. عِجْلًا is the object. جَسَداً is a naʿt (adjective). لَهُ خُوارٌ is nominative by the mubtadaʾ-construction or by the attribute. One says خار يخور خوارا when it lows, and likewise جأر يجأر جؤارا; and one says خار يخور خورا when one is cowardly and weak. اتَّخَذُوهُ: the second object is omitted, i.e. "they took it as a god".

nahhas-irab:149-149.t: Al-Akhfash said: one says سقط في يده and أسقط. Whoever says سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ, the meaning in his view is "regret fell". قالوا لئن لم ترحمنا ربّنا is a condition containing the sense of an oath, and ربّنا is on the vocative. Whoever reads يَرْحَمْنا with the yāʾ and وَيَغْفِرْ لَنا with the yāʾ, رَبُّنا is nominative by its verb; and whoever reads ترحمنا with the tāʾ and تغفر لنا with the tāʾ makes ربّنا accusative as a vocative in construct, as though he said: "O our Lord".

nahhas-irab:150-150.t:
غَضْبانَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is a diptote because its feminine is غضبى. The real reason for its being a diptote is that the alif and nūn in it are in the position of the two alifs of the feminine in your saying حمراء, the nūn being a substitute, as is said of صنعاء: صنعانيّ. أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ: Yaʿqūb said: one says عجلت الشيء ("I outstripped the thing") and أعجلت الرجل ("I hastened the man"). وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ: أخذ برأسه and أخذ رأسه are one, and likewise وَامْسَحُوا بِرُؤُسِكُمْ [al-Māʾida: 6]. It was said: he took hold of his head only by way of confiding a secret, nothing else, and Hārūn ﷺ disliked that those present should imagine [otherwise], because the matter was other than that; so he said ابن أمّ ("son of my mother") seeking his compassion, for he was his brother through his mother; and this is found in the speech of the Arabs, as he said: [al-Khafīf] 160-
يا ابن أمّي ويا شقيق نفسي
(O son of my mother, O full brother of my soul.)
The people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr read ابْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ الْقَوْمَ, and the people of Kufa read ابْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ الْقَوْمَ [i.e. أُمِّ]. Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd said: يا ابن أمَّ is construed as يا ابن أمّاه. The Basrans said: this view is a mistake, because the alif is light and is not dropped; rather the two nouns were made one noun, so it became like your saying: خمسة عشر أقبلوا. Al-Akhfash and Abū Ḥātim said: يا ابن أمِّ, as one says: يا غلام غلامِ أقبل. Abū Jaʿfar said: يا غلام غلامِ is an anomalous dialect form, because the second is not addressed, so the yāʾ should not be dropped from it; thus the reading with kasra on the mīm is far-fetched on this view, but it has a good, fine construal: it is in the position of your saying يا خمسة عشر أقبلوا — when he made the two nouns one noun, he annexed it. إِنَّ الْقَوْمَ اسْتَضْعَفُونِي وَكادُوا يَقْتُلُونَنِي is with two nūns because it is an imperfect verb, and assimilation is permissible outside the Qurʾān. Mujāhid and Mālik ibn Dīnār read فَلا تُشْمِتْ بِيَ الْأَعْداءَ [i.e. فلا تَشْمَتْ بي الأعداءُ] with the tāʾ, treating the group as feminine; kasra on it [the mīm] is permissible, and the masculine is permissible on [the sense of] the plural. There is a subtle point in it: one may ask, how can the enemies be forbidden from gloating? The answer is that this is like His saying, Mighty and Exalted: فَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ [al-Baqara: 132], i.e. remain firm in Islam until death comes to you; and as the Arabs say: لا أرينك هاهنا ("let me not see you here"). The meaning is "do not do to me something on account of which the enemies would gloat". Abū ʿUbayd said: and it was related from Ḥumayd فَلا تُشْمِتْ with kasra on the mīm. Abū Jaʿfar said: there is no construal for this reading, because if it is from شمت he would have to say تَشْمَت, and if it is from أشمت he would have to say تُشْمِت. [Translator's note: the vocalisations in this passage are not marked in the source; they are supplied here from the sense.]

nahhas-irab:151-151.t: قالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِأَخِي: he repeated the preposition because a genitive pronoun is not conjoined to except in this way, except in anomalous cases, as Ḥamza read تساءلون به والأرحام [al-Nisāʾ: 1]; on that basis اغفر لي وأخي would come.

nahhas-irab:152-152.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ is the noun of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is سَيَنالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ; wrath from Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is punishment. وَذِلَّةٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا: because they were commanded to kill one another, and they saw that they had gone astray. What best fits the context of the speech is that إنّ الذين اتخذوا العجل سينالهم غضب من ربهم وذلة في الحياة الدنيا is part of the speech of Moses ﷺ, which Allah, Mighty and Exalted, reported from him, and the speech is complete; then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُفْتَرِينَ.

nahhas-irab:153-153.t: وَالَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السَّيِّئاتِ is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِها لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ, i.e. "to them".

nahhas-irab:154-154.t: وَفِي نُسْخَتِها هُدىً is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). وَرَحْمَةٌ is conjoined to it. لِلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ: there are three views on the lām. The view of the Kufans is that it is redundant (zāʾida); al-Kisāʾī said: someone who heard al-Farazdaq told me that he said: نقدت لها مائة درهم ("I paid for her a hundred dirhams"), meaning نقدتها. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a maṣdar. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: some said the meaning is "and those who, for the sake of their Lord, are in awe".

nahhas-irab:155-155.t:
وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا: two objects, from one of which «من» has been dropped. Sībawayh recited:
[al-Ṭawīl] 161-
[و] منّا الّذي اختير الرّجال سماحة ... وجودا إذا هبّ الرّياح الزّعازع
(And from us is the one who was chosen from among men for generosity and liberality when the violent winds blow.)
فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ: i.e. they died. قالَ رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أَهْلَكْتَهُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ: i.e. You would have caused them to die, as He, Mighty and Exalted, said: إِنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ [al-Nisāʾ: 176]. وَإِيَّايَ is conjoined; the meaning is: had You willed, You would have caused us to die before going out to the appointed meeting, so people would not imagine of us that we had brought about a departure from obedience to You.
أَتُهْلِكُنا بِما فَعَلَ السُّفَهاءُ مِنَّا إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِها مَنْ تَشاءُ وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشاءُ أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنا فَاغْفِرْ لَنا وَارْحَمْنا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْغافِرِينَ: an interrogative carrying the sense of negation; thus it is in the speech of the Arabs, and when it is a negation [interrogated] it has the sense of affirmation, as Jarīr said: [al-Wāfir] 162-
ألستم خير من ركب المطايا ... وأندى العالمين بطون راح
(Are you not the best of those who have ridden mounts, and the most generous of all the worlds in the palms of their hands?)
إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ: i.e. this is nothing but Your testing and Your imposing on us what is hard. تُضِلُّ بِها مَنْ تَشاءُ: i.e. You lead astray by it those whom You will, and those whom You will are those who do not endure patiently in affliction and are not content. وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشاءُ: whoever endures patiently and is content. أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنا is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْغافِرِينَ.

nahhas-irab:156-156.t: Abū Wajza al-Saʿdī read إِنَّا هُدْنا إِلَيْكَ [i.e. هِدْنا]. One says هاد يهود — this is the well-known form — when one repents; and one says ثوب مهوّد, i.e. thinned and softened. قالَ عَذابِي أُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ أَشاءُ: i.e. those whom I will, i.e. those deserving of it. وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ: i.e. whoever enters into it, it is not incapable of [encompassing] him; and it was said: it encompasses every thing of creation, so that even a beast has mercy and tenderness toward its young.

nahhas-irab:157-157.t: الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ is genitive as a badal (substitute) of the first «الذين», and if you wish it is a naʿt (adjective); and likewise الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ. «والذين هم» is conjoined. Abū Jaʿfar, Ayyūb, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read وضع عنهم آصارهم, which is the plural of إصر. Its root meaning in the language is weight, and it is what they were made to worship by of what is heavy. It was said: it is what they were obliged to do of cutting off whatever urine had touched; and it was said: it is the covenants that were taken from them, that they would obey Allah, Mighty and Exalted, believe in His prophets, the blessings of Allah be upon them, befriend the people of obedience and be hostile to the people of disobedience, whether near or far. Al-Akhfash said: al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā read وَعَزَّرُوهُ lightened [i.e. وعَزَرُوه], and likewise وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ [al-Māʾida: 12]. Abū Isḥāq said: one says عزره يعزره and يعزره [i.e. يَعْزِرُه / يَعْزُرُه].

nahhas-irab:159-159.t: It may refer to those of them who believed, and it may refer to a people who have perished, or to those who joined ʿĪsā ﷺ and believed in him. The meaning of يهدون بالحق is: they call people to guidance; وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ: in judgement.

nahhas-irab:160-160.t: وَقَطَّعْناهُمُ اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْباطاً: the implied structure is "twelve communities", and for this reason the feminine is permitted. أَسْباطاً is a badal (substitute) of اثنتي عشرة. أُمَماً is a naʿt (adjective) of أسباط. The meaning is: We made them twelve groups.

nahhas-irab:161-162.t: Maʿmar related from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ: he said: they said, "A grain in a hair." Abū al-Qāsim Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Qazwīnī narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī narrated to us: Sufyān informed us, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayra: they said, "A grain in a hair"; and it was said to them وَادْخُلُوا الْبابَ سُجَّداً, but they entered shuffling on their backsides. بِما كانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ: [يظلمون] is nominative because it is an imperfect verb, and its position is accusative [as khabar of كان]; «ما» has the sense of the maṣdar, i.e. "for their wrongdoing".

nahhas-irab:163-163.t: وَسْئَلْهُمْ عَنِ الْقَرْيَةِ: if you lighten the hamza you say وسلهم, casting its vowel onto the sīn and dropping it. الَّتِي is in the position of the genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of «القرية». إِذْ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is "ask them about the time when they transgressed on the Sabbath", and this is a question of rebuke and affirmation. يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَيَوْمَ لا يَسْبِتُونَ: we have mentioned the view of al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayd that the meaning of يسبتون is "they venerate the Sabbath"; its reality in the language is "they do the deed of the Sabbath". One says سبت يسبت when one rests or does the deed of the Sabbath. Most Arabs say اليومَ السبتُ and likewise الجمعة [i.e. with اليوم in the accusative], because there is an action in both of them; and of the rest of the days you say, with the nominative: اليومُ الاثنان. The implied structure is "and they do not come to them on a day when they do not keep the Sabbath". The adverb is annexed to the verb, according to Sībawayh because of their frequent use of it, and according to Abū al-ʿAbbās because the verb has the sense of the maṣdar. Abū Isḥāq said: it is by way of quotation (ḥikāya), i.e. "a day on which this is said". According to Sībawayh, لا يفعل is the negation of ليفعلنّ, or of هو يفعل when the future is intended. كَذلِكَ نَبْلُوهُمْ: i.e. We are severe on them in [their] worship and test them; the kāf is in the position of the accusative. بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ: i.e. for their defiant disobedience.

nahhas-irab:164-164.t:
وَإِذْ قالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنْهُمْ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوْماً: the original is «لما»; the alif was dropped because it is an interrogative. And it was said: «ما» [i.e. the lām] is a genitive particle. [Translator's note: as printed; the sense is that the lām is the genitive particle governing «ما».] If you pause outside the Qurʾān you say لمه, the hāʾ being to show the vowel.
قالُوا مَعْذِرَةً إِلى رَبِّكُمْ: ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read مَعْذِرَةً in the accusative. Its accusative, according to al-Kisāʾī, is from two angles: one of them is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the other is that the implied structure is "we did that as an excuse".
Sībawayh distinguished between the nominative and the accusative and made clear that the nominative is the preferred choice. He said: because they did not intend to excuse themselves with a fresh excuse for something for which they might be blamed; rather, it was said to them, "Why do you admonish?" and they said, "Our admonition is an excuse"; whereas if a man said to a man, معذرةً إلى الله وإليك من كذا وكذا, intending an act of excusing himself, he would use the accusative. This is among the subtleties and fine points of Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, in which he is not matched.

nahhas-irab:165-165.t:
الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا بِعَذابٍ بَئِيسٍ: there are eleven readings of this,
and i'rab is more deserving of mentioning them because of the grammar in them, and because only the people of i'rab can establish the like of them precisely. Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read بِعَذابٍ بَئِيسٍ on the pattern faʿīl. The people of Mecca read بِعَذابٍ بَئِيسٍ with kasra on the bāʾ [i.e. بِئِيس], the pattern being the same. The people of Medina read بِعَذابٍ بَئِيسٍ with the bāʾ with kasra followed by an unvowelled yāʾ and the sīn with kasra and tanwīn [i.e. بِيسٍ]. Al-Ḥasan read بعذاب بئس بما, the bāʾ with kasra followed by an unvowelled hamza and the sīn with fatḥa [i.e. بِئْسَ]. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ read بعذاب بئس, the bāʾ with fatḥa, the hamza with kasra and the sīn with kasra and tanwīn [i.e. بَئِسٍ]. Yaʿqūb the reader said, from one of the readers: بعذاب بئس, the bāʾ with fatḥa, the hamza with kasra and the sīn with fatḥa [i.e. بَئِسَ]. Al-Aʿmash read بعذاب بيئس on the pattern fayʿil; it is related from him بيأس on the pattern fayʿal; and it is related from him بعذاب بئّس with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a doubled hamza with kasra — the sīn in all of this having kasra and tanwīn, meaning the reading of al-Aʿmash. Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read بعذاب بيّس, the bāʾ with fatḥa followed by a doubled yāʾ, without hamza. Yaʿqūb the reader said: and it came from one of the readers بعذاب بئيس, the bāʾ with kasra followed by an unvowelled hamza, followed by a yāʾ with fatḥa [i.e. بِئْيَس]. These are eleven readings.
Whoever read بَئِيسٍ takes it in his view from بؤس فهو بئيس, i.e. it became severe; and likewise بِئِيس, except that he gave the bāʾ kasra because it is followed by a hamza with kasra. As for the reading of the people of Medina, there are three views on it. Al-Kisāʾī said: its construal is بئيس, then the hamza was lightened as the people of Medina do, so two yāʾs came together, which was heavy, so they dropped one of them and cast its vowel onto the bāʾ, and it became بيس. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the original is بَئِس, then the bāʾ was given kasra because of the kasra of the hamza, so it became بِئِس, then the kasra was dropped from the hamza because of its heaviness. These are two views. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: the Arabs say جاء ببنات بيس, i.e. "he brought something bad", so the meaning of «بعذاب بيس» is "with a bad punishment".
As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥātim claimed that it has no construal; he said: because one does not say مررت برجل بئس until one says بئس الرجل or بئس رجلا. Abū Jaʿfar said: this statement of Abū Ḥātim is rejected; the grammarians related إن فعلت كذا وكذا فيها ونعمت, meaning ونعمت الخصلة ("and an excellent trait it is"); so the implied structure on al-Ḥasan's reading is "with a punishment — wretched is the punishment"; and بعذاب بَئِس is on the pattern faʿil, like حذر. The reading of al-Aʿmash, بيئس, is not permissible according to the view of the Basrans, because the like of this does not occur in the speech of the Arabs except in the weak, assimilated [roots], such as ميّت and سيّد. As for بيأس, it is permissible according to them, because its like is صيرف and حيدر. As for بئّس, its like is hardly known among adjectives. As for بيّس without hamza, it occurs only in yāʾ-roots, such as بيّع. As for بئيس [i.e. بِئْيَس], it is permissible, and its like is جذيم [i.e. حِذْيَم]. [Translator's note: the source prints "As for بيأس, it is permissible" a second time at the end; given the preceding enumeration, the last form is presumably the eleventh reading بِئْيَس.]

nahhas-irab:166-166.t: فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا عَنْ ما نُهُوا: i.e. when they went beyond bounds in disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Exalted. قُلْنا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خاسِئِينَ: one says خسأته فخسأ, i.e. I drove him away and banished him.

nahhas-irab:168-168.t: مِنْهُمُ الصَّالِحُونَ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذلِكَ is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and we know of no one who made it nominative.

nahhas-irab:169-169.t: وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغْفَرُ لَنا: assimilating the rāʾ into the lām is not permissible, because there is repetition (trilling) in it; assimilating the lām into the rāʾ is permissible, as in بَلْ رانَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 14]. وَإِنْ يَأْتِهِمْ is jussive (majzūm) by the condition, so the yāʾ was dropped from it, and the apodosis is يَأْخُذُوهُ. Al-Kisāʾī said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read وادّارسوا ما فيه, assimilating the tāʾ into the dāl.

nahhas-irab:170-170.t:
وَالَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ بِالْكِتابِ is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the construal of its khabar (predicate) is إِنَّا لا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُصْلِحِينَ "of them". Abū al-ʿĀliya and ʿĀṣim read وَالَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ بِالْكِتابِ [i.e. يُمْسِكُون]; but the speech of the Arabs is otherwise: they say مسّكت and أمسكته, and likewise the reading وَلا تُمْسِكُوا بِعِصَمِ الْكَوافِرِ [al-Mumtaḥana: 10]; and Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said, bringing it according to its nature: [al-Basīṭ] 163-
فما تمسّك بالحبل الذي زعمت ... إلّا كما تمسك الماء الغرابيل
(She does not hold to the bond she claimed, except as sieves hold water.)
[Translator's note: the passage as printed is unclear about which form is the standard one.]

nahhas-irab:171-171.t: وَإِذْ نَتَقْنَا الْجَبَلَ: i.e. "and remind them". فَوْقَهُمْ is an adverb (ẓarf). ظُلَّةٌ is the khabar of «كأنّ»; and «أنّ» [in وظنّوا أنّه واقع بهم] is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the kāf is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. And the "barr" is construed according to the meaning. [Translator's note: the last two sentences appear garbled in the source; «والبر» may be a corruption.]

nahhas-irab:172-173.t:
وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ in the sense of "and remember". This ayah is difficult, and we have mentioned something about it. Some people said: the meaning of وإذ أخذ ربّك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرّيّاتهم is that He brought forth from the backs of the children of Adam some of them from others; they said: and the meaning of وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ is "He said". In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ there is other than this view. Abū Jaʿfar said: it was read to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad while I was listening, from Qutayba, from Mālik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Abī Unaysa, that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed him, from Muslim ibn Yasār al-Juhanī, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about this ayah: وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قالُوا بَلى شَهِدْنا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هذا غافِلِينَ. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being asked about it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Exalted, created Adam, then stroked his back with His right hand and brought forth from it offspring, and said: 'I created these for Paradise, and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise.' Then He stroked his back and brought forth from it offspring, and said: 'I created these for the Fire, and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire.'" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds?"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies upon a deed of the people of Paradise, and He admits him into Paradise; and when He creates a servant for the Fire, He employs him in the deeds of the people of the Fire until he dies, and He admits him into the Fire." He said: and Allah the Exalted is not unjust to him in this case, because He already knew what would come from him. Abū Jaʿfar said: the ayah is nevertheless difficult, and we will examine thoroughly what is in it. One of the scholars said: it is specific, because Allah, Mighty and Exalted, said: مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ, so excluded from this are those who were the direct children of Adam, upon him be peace, from his own loins. And He, Mighty and Exalted, said: أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّما أَشْرَكَ آباؤُنا مِنْ قَبْلُ, so excluded from it is everyone who did not have idolatrous fathers. The meaning of وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ is: He said [it] to them by sending a messenger to them. And it was said:
Rather, it is general to all people, because everyone knows that he was a child who was fed and raised, and that he has a Disposer and a Creator; this is the meaning of وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ, and the meaning of قالُوا بَلى is that this is binding upon them. And it was said: this is for those who came from the backs of the children of Adam, upon him be peace, and it is known that the direct children of Adam, upon him be peace, were such. [Translator's note: the last clause is elliptical in the source.]
The people of Medina and the people of Kufa read (أن تقولوا) with the tāʾ dotted above; and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, Ibn Muḥayṣin, ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read أن يقولوا with the yāʾ. (أن) is in the position of the accusative in both readings, in the sense of "out of aversion that", and according to the Kufans in the sense of "lest". أَفَتُهْلِكُنا بِما فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ, in the sense of "You do not do this".

nahhas-irab:175-175.t: وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ is in the position of the jussive according to the Kufans, and for that reason the wāw was dropped from it; al-Farrāʾ said: and the jussive lām is omitted. According to the Basrans it is indeclinable (mabnī), on the original state of verbs. فَأَتْبَعَهُ الشَّيْطانُ فَكانَ مِنَ الْغاوِينَ: i.e. of the treacherous.

nahhas-irab:176-176.t: وَلَوْ شِئْنا لَرَفَعْناهُ بِها: i.e. had We willed, We would have caused him to die before he disobeyed, and raised him to Paradise by them, i.e. by acting on them. فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الْكَلْبِ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It was said: «مثل» here means "description", as He said: مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ [al-Raʿd: 35]; and it was said: it is in its proper sense. إِنْ تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ is a condition and its apodosis, and it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "his likeness is that of the dog, panting". The meaning is that he is in one state, not desisting from disobedience, like the dog whose condition is this. And it was said: the meaning is that he does not desist from harming people, like the dog, panting. The meaning of لاهث is that it moves its tongue and barks. In this ayah is the greatest benefit for whoever reflects on it, namely that it contains a prohibition of blind imitation (taqlīd) of a scholar except with a proof that he makes clear, because Allah, Mighty and Exalted, reported that He gave this man His signs and he cast them off, so it is necessary to fear the like of this for others, and that nothing be accepted from him except with a proof.

nahhas-irab:177-177.t: ساءَ مَثَلًا الْقَوْمُ: al-Akhfash said: He made "the likeness of the people" figurative (majāz). The implied structure is "evil as a likeness is the likeness of the people"; الْقَوْمُ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or on an implied mubtadaʾ. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī and al-Aʿmash read (ساء مثل القوم), making مثل nominative by ساء.

nahhas-irab:178-178.t: مَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِي is a condition and its apodosis, and likewise وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ.

nahhas-irab:179-179.t: I.e. they are in the position of one who does not understand, because they do not benefit from them. أُولئِكَ كَالْأَنْعامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ: بَلْ here is not a retraction of the first; rather the meaning is: they are like cattle, and they are more astray than cattle, because they are not guided to reward.

nahhas-irab:180-180.t: This is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī [i.e. يُلْحِدُون]; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read يلحدون with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ. The eloquent usage is ألحد في دينه ("he deviated in his religion") and لحد القبر ("he dug the niche of the grave"), but each of them may enter upon the other, because the meaning is the meaning of inclining. The meaning of "they deviate concerning His names" is of two kinds: one is that they name something other than Him a god, and the other is that they call Him by names other than His names.

nahhas-irab:181-181.t: Allah, Mighty and Exalted, indicated by this ayah that the world is never, at any time, without a caller who calls to the truth.

nahhas-irab:182-183.t: وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ: the plotting (kayd) of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is His punishment when it comes upon them from where they do not perceive; this is the meaning of kayd in the language.

nahhas-irab:185-185.t: وَأَنْ عَسى is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to what precedes it. (أن يكون) is in the position of the nominative.

nahhas-irab:186-186.t: مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ: condition and requital. وَنَذَرُهُمْ with the nūn is the reading of the people of Medina, and there are two construals of it: one of them is that it is conjoined to what is required after the fāʾ in the requital, and likewise «ونذرهم». The reading of the Kufans is وَيَذَرُهُمْ with the yāʾ, and the jussive is conjoined to the position of the fāʾ. [Translator's note: only one of the "two construals" is stated in the source.] The meaning is: He does not cause them to die when they disobey until their appointed term arrives.

nahhas-irab:187-187.t: يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ: i.e. about the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place. أَيَّانَ مُرْساها: i.e. they say: when will it occur? مُرْساها is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh, and by an implied verb according to Abū al-ʿAbbās. مُرساها is from أرساها, and مَرساها is from رست, i.e. it became fixed and occurred; and from it is وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ [Sabaʾ: 13]; Qatāda said: i.e. fixed. قُلْ إِنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ رَبِّي is mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate). لا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلَّا بَغْتَةً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). يَسْئَلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْها: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the view of the exegetes that the meaning involves fronting and postponement. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the meaning is "they ask you as though you were persistent in asking about it", i.e. insistent; he holds that there is no fronting or postponement in it. One says أحفى في المسألة وفي الطلب, so he is محفٍ, and حفيّ for intensity, like مخصب and خصيب. قُلْ إِنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ اللَّهِ: this is not a repetition; rather one of the two "knowledges" is of its occurrence, and the other of its essence [lit. "of its kunh"]. [Translator's note: the source prints «لكنها», presumably a corruption of «لكُنْهِها».]

nahhas-irab:188-188.t:
ما شاءَ اللَّهُ is in the position of the accusative as an exception; the meaning is "except what Allah wills to give me power over". Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 164-
مهما شاء بالناس يفعل
(Whatever he wills, he does with people.)
وَلَوْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ لَاسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ وَما مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ: among the best of what has been said about it is that the meaning is: if I knew the unseen — what Allah, Mighty and Exalted, wants from me — before He makes it known to me, I would do it. And it was said:
If I knew when victory in war would be mine, I would fight and not be defeated.

nahhas-irab:189-189.t: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and we have mentioned it. It was said that the meaning is: He is the One who created you from Adam, upon him be peace; then [وَجَعَلَ مِنْها زَوْجَها] He made from him his wife — a report. فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّاها حَمَلَتْ حَمْلًا خَفِيفاً: everything that is in the belly is ḥaml with fatḥa, and when it is on the back it is ḥiml; and what is on the palm tree is ḥaml with fatḥa, though Yaʿqūb related kasra for the fruit of the palm tree. Al-Akhfash said: فَلَمَّا أَثْقَلَتْ: she became possessed of heaviness, as you say أثمر النخل ("the palms bore fruit"). لَئِنْ آتَيْتَنا صالِحاً: i.e. sound in form.

nahhas-irab:190-190.t: فَلَمَّا آتاهُما صالِحاً: it was said the implied structure is "a sound giving", and it was male and female, as Ḥawwāʾ used to give birth. جَعَلا لَهُ: it was said it means the disbelieving male and female, and by it He means the two sexes; this is indicated by فَتَعالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ, where He did not say يشركان; this is a good view. And it was said: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ — from one form and one shape — وَجَعَلَ مِنْها زَوْجَها, i.e. from its kind; فلمّا تغشّاها means the two sexes; and on this view Adam and Ḥawwāʾ are not mentioned in the ayah. The people of Medina and ʿĀṣim read جعلا له شركا, and Abū ʿAmr and the rest of the people of Kufa read جَعَلا لَهُ شُرَكاءَ. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd rejected the first reading and said: on this reading it ought to be "they gave to another than Him a share", because they acknowledge that the root [of the thing] belongs to Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and they only give a share to another than Him. Abū Jaʿfar said: the interpretation for whoever reads the first reading is "they made for Him one possessing a share", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82].

nahhas-irab:193-193.t: وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدى لا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ: al-Akhfash said: and if you call the idols to guidance, they will not follow you. سَواءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صامِتُونَ: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: because it is the end of an ayah — meaning that He said «أم أنتم صامتون» and did not say أم صمتم. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of «أم أنتم صامتون» and of «أم صمتم» is the same; this is the view of Sībawayh.

nahhas-irab:194-194.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ is the noun of إنّ. عِبادٌ is its khabar (predicate). أَمْثالُكُمْ is a naʿt (adjective). Abū Ḥātim Sahl ibn Muḥammad al-Sijistānī related that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read إنِ الذين تدعون من دون الله عبادا أمثالكم, with «إن» lightened and given kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters, «عبادا» accusative with tanwīn, and «أمثالكم» accusative. He said: he means "those whom you call upon besides Allah are not servants like you", i.e. they are stones, idols and wood. Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading ought not to be read, from three angles. One of them is that it contradicts the written text (al-sawād). The second is that Sībawayh chooses the nominative in the khabar of «إن» when it has the sense of «ما», saying إن زيد منطلق, because the governing power of «ما» is weak, and «إن» having its meaning is weaker than it. The third angle is that al-Kisāʾī claimed that «إن» hardly ever occurs in the speech of the Arabs in the sense of «ما» unless it is followed by an affirmation, as He, Mighty and Exalted, said: إِنِ الْكافِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ [al-Mulk: 20].
فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ: the original is for the lām to have kasra; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness and because the lām is joined to what precedes it. إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ: [صادقين] is the khabar of كنتم. There is an omission in the speech [lit. "in the lām"]; the meaning is "so call them to follow you, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful that they are gods". [Translator's note: «وفي اللام حذف» is as printed; the context suggests «وفي الكلام حذف».]

nahhas-irab:195-195.t: أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِها: you are superior to them, so how do you [worship] them? [Translator's note: «فكيف تجدونهم» as printed; perhaps a corruption of «فكيف تعبدونهم».] Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍ يَبْطِشُونَ [i.e. يَبْطُشُون], and it is a dialect form. اليد ("hand"), الرّجل ("foot") and الأذن ("ear") are feminine and are diminished with the hāʾ, and a yāʾ is added to اليد in the diminutive, restoring it to its original form. قُلِ ادْعُوا شُرَكاءَكُمْ: i.e. those whom you made partners and to whom you gave a portion of your wealth. ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ: the original is كيدوني with the yāʾ; the yāʾ was dropped because the kasra indicates it; and likewise فَلا تُنْظِرُونِ, i.e. "and do not grant me respite".

nahhas-irab:196-196.t: إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ: the noun of «إنّ» and its khabar (predicate). ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read إنّ وليَّ اللهُ الذي نزّل الكتاب, meaning Jibrīl, upon him be peace. The meaning of وليّي الله is "my Protector and my Helper is Allah"; the walī of a thing is the one who protects it and keeps harm from it.

nahhas-irab:197-197.t: وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَكُمْ.

nahhas-irab:198-198.t:
وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدى is a condition, so the nūn was dropped from it, and the apodosis is لا يَسْمَعُوا.
وَتَراهُمْ is resumptive. يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning of looking (naẓar) is opening the eyes toward the thing looked at, and it is not like seeing. They are spoken of with the wāw [of the masculine plural] because the report runs on the action of rational beings.

nahhas-irab:199-199.t: خُذِ الْعَفْوَ: it is the little/easy amount. Abū ʿAbd Allāh Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad said: al-ʿafw is zakāt, because it is a little out of much. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is from عفا when something is effaced; and one may say "take the ʿafw from him", i.e. do not be hard on him, and be lenient with him. وَأْمُرْ بِالْعُرْفِ: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read بِالْعُرْفِ [i.e. بالعُرُف], i.e. what is recognised as good (al-maʿrūf); the meaning of al-maʿrūf is what is good according to reason. وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْجاهِلِينَ: i.e. when you have established the proof against them and commanded them what is right, and they behave ignorantly toward you, turn away from them, to protect yourself from them and to raise your rank above answering them. [Translator's note: «صيانة له» as printed, literally "to protect him".]

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
المص كِتابٌ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ: al-Kisāʾī said: that is, "this is a Book sent down to you". Al-Farrāʾ said:
the meaning is: alif, lām, mīm and ṣād, of the disjointed letters, [are] a Book sent down to you, gathered together. Abū Isḥāq said: this view is wrong in three respects. One is that if it were as he said, these letters would always have to be followed by "Book", but Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has said: الم اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ [Āl ʿImrān: 1–2]. Another is that if it were as he said, «الم» would not be in more than one place, nor «حم». Another is that he has implied two things, because he needs to take «الم» as some of the letters of "a Book sent down to you"; and this is not like your saying "ا ب ت ث are twenty-eight letters", because this is a name for the [whole] sura, as you say "al-Ḥamd is seven verses"; the proof of this is that one may not say "ط ظ ر ن are twenty-eight letters". Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Farrāʾ did permit this. فَلا يَكُنْ: a prohibition; the sign of the jussive in it is the dropping of the ḍamma from the nūn, and the wāw was dropped because it is quiescent and the nūn is quiescent; it was the more fitting to drop because it is preceded by a ḍamma that indicates it. حَرَجٌ: the noun of يكن; the prohibition in wording is directed at the حرج and in meaning at the one addressed. لِتُنْذِرَ بِهِ: accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay). وَذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: a diptote because there is an alif of the feminine at its end; it may be in the position of the nominative, the accusative or the genitive. The nominative is, according to the Basrans, on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); al-Kisāʾī said: it is conjoined to «كتاب». The accusative is, according to the Basrans, as a maṣdar (verbal noun); al-Kisāʾī said: it is conjoined to the hāʾ in «أنزلناه» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has أُنزل إليك]. The genitive is in the sense of "for warning and a reminder for the believers", genitive by the lām.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: اتَّبِعُوا: an imperative; it is jussive according to al-Farrāʾ and indeclinable (mabnī) according to Sībawayh. وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا: jussive. مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ: an object, a diptote because it contains the alif of the feminine; that is, do not worship another besides Him. قَلِيلًا: a naʿt (adjective) of an adverb or of a maṣdar. ما تَذَكَّرُونَ: «ما» may be redundant (zāʾida), or it may form a maṣdar together with the verb. The original form is تتذكّرون; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl because it is close to it. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read تذكرون, dropping the second tāʾ because two tāʾs come together.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَكَمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها: in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the accusative by an implied verb is also permissible.
فَجاءَها بَأْسُنا بَياتاً أَوْ هُمْ قائِلُونَ: al-Farrāʾ said: the wāw was dropped for lightness, and the meaning is أو وهم قائلون. Abū Isḥāq said: this is wrong; when a referring pronoun is present the wāw is dispensed with. You say جاءني زيد راكبا أو هو ماش ("Zayd came to me riding, or he walking") and there is no need for the wāw.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: فَما كانَ دَعْواهُمْ: the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and its noun is إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا.

nahhas-irab:6-7.t: By this He indicated that the unbelievers will be called to account. This is the lām of the oath, and in reality it is for emphasis, and likewise فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِعِلْمٍ. وَما كُنَّا غائِبِينَ: the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the governing effect of ما is cancelled.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: وَالْوَزْنُ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). الْحَقُّ: its khabar (predicate). الحق may also be its naʿt (adjective), with the khabar being يَوْمَئِذٍ. The accusative of الحق as a maṣdar (verbal noun) is also permissible. فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb), and likewise وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ. بِما كانُوا بِآياتِنا يَظْلِمُونَ: a maṣdar, that is, "because of their wrongdoing".

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
Al-Aʿraj read معائش with a hamza, and so Khārija ibn Muṣʿab transmitted from Nāfiʿ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the hamza is a solecism (laḥn) and is not permissible, because the singular is معيشة; you add the alif of the plural, which is quiescent, and the yāʾ is quiescent, so one of them must be given a vowel, since there is no way to drop either, and the alif cannot take a vowel; so the yāʾ was given the vowel it should have in the singular. Its parallel with wāw is منارة and مناور, مقامة and مقاوم, as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 144-
وإنّي لقوّام مقاوم لم يكن ... جرير ولا مولى جرير يقومها
(I am one who stands up in standing-places where neither Jarīr nor Jarīr's client would stand.)
Likewise مصيبة and مصاوب; this is the good form, and مصايب is an anomalous dialect form. Al-Akhfash said: مصايب is permissible only because the singular is weak (muʿtall). Abū Isḥāq said: this is wrong; it would oblige him to say مقايم. Rather, the view in my opinion is that it is like وسادة and إسادة.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already discussed the meaning of وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْناكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْناكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ: an exception from an affirmative statement. لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ: in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: قالَ ما مَنَعَكَ: ما is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); according to al-Kisāʾī [it is nominative] by the returning pronoun. The meaning is "what thing prevented you". أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ: in the position of the accusative, that is, "from prostrating". قالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ: mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate). There are three dialect forms of أنا, the most eloquent being أنا فعلت with the alif dropped in continuous speech, because it is added to show the vowel in pausing. Al-Farrāʾ said: some of Banū Qays and Rabīʿa say أنا فعلت, retaining the alif in continuous speech. Al-Kisāʾī said: some of Quḍāʿa say أان فعلت, like عان. In pausing there are three forms, the most eloquent being أنا. Al-Kisāʾī said: among the Arabs are those who say «أنه». Al-Akhfash said: among the Arabs are those who say «أن» in pausing.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t:
قالَ فَبِما أَغْوَيْتَنِي: there are three answers concerning it: it may be from الغيّ (error); it may be like أحمدت الرجل ("I found the man praiseworthy") [i.e. "You found me astray"]; and it has also been said: أغواه means "he disappointed him". لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِراطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ, that is, "I will lie in wait for them in error on Your path"; «على» was omitted, as Sībawayh reported: ضرب الظّهر والبطن ("he was struck on the back and the belly"), and he recited: [al-Kāmil] 145-
لدن بهزّ الكفّ يعسل متنه ... فيه كما عسل الطّريق الثّعلب
(Supple [spear]; at the shaking of the palm its shaft quivers, as the fox runs quivering along the road.)
The implied form is على صراطك and في صراطك. The religion is called a path (صراط) because it is the road to salvation.
The best that has been said about the meaning of ثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمانِهِمْ وَعَنْ شَمائِلِهِمْ is: in misguidance. [Translator's note: the sentence is elliptical in the source.]

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: قالَ اخْرُجْ مِنْها مَذْؤُماً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, read لَمَنْ تَبِعَكَ with a kasra on the lām [Translator's note: i.e. لِمَن; the printed vowelling shows the fatḥa].
