Some grammarians rejected it; its implied form — and Allah knows best — is "on account of those who follow you", as one says أكرمت فلانا لك ("I honoured so-and-so on your account"). The meaning may also be: "the expulsion is for those of them who follow you". Abū Isḥāq said: whoever reads «لمن تبعك» with a fatḥa on the lām, for him it is a lām of the oath, preparing the way for His saying لَأَمْلَأَنَّ. Others said: in لمن تبعك it is a lām of emphasis, and in لأملأنّ a lām of the oath; the proof of this is that outside the Qur'an the first lām may be omitted but the second may not. The passage carries the sense of condition and requital, that is, "whoever follows you, I will punish him"; if you said من تبعك أعذبه it would not be permissible unless you meant لأعذبنه.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t:
وَلا تَقْرَبا هذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ: a prohibition. فَتَكُونا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ: an answer [to the prohibition]; it may also be conjoined.
Al-Akhfash said: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا, that is, "to them". ما وُورِيَ: outside the Qur'an أوري is permissible, like «أقّتت». إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ: the khabar (predicate) of تكونا; «أن» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of "for fear", and the Kufans say: [in the sense of] "lest". Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ with a kasra on the lām [Translator's note: i.e. مَلِكَين, "two kings"; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading]; on this reading a sukūn on it is also permissible, but not on the first reading, because of the lightness of the fatḥa. Abū ʿUbayd claimed that Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr's citing as evidence His saying وَمُلْكٍ لا يَبْلى [Ṭā Hā: 120] is a clear proof, "but people have abandoned it, so we have abandoned it". Abū Jaʿfar said: إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ [with kasra] is an anomalous reading, and these words of Abū ʿUbayd were objected to and counted a gross error. Could Adam ﷺ have imagined that he would attain more than the dominion of Paradise, which is the ultimate goal of seekers? The meaning of وَمُلْكٍ لا يَبْلى is only remaining in the dominion of Paradise and abiding eternally in it. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has made clear the superiority of the angels over all creation in more than one place in the Qur'an: among them this one, إلّا أن يكونا ملكين; among them وَلا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ [al-Anʿām: 50]; and among them لَا الْمَلائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ [al-Nisāʾ: 172]. Al-Ḥasan said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, favoured the angels with forms, wings and honour. Others said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, favoured them with obedience and the abandonment of disobedience, and it is by this that preference occurs in everything.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
«لكما» is not included in the ṣila (relative clause), and the grammarians have three views on it. Hishām said: the implied form is "I am a sincere adviser to you; [I am] indeed of the sincere advisers". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: لكما may be explanatory, as you say مرحبا بك and بك مرحبا. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said that al-Māzinī said — and it is my preference — that the alif and lām are as they are in الرجل and are not in the sense of الذي; do you not see that you say نعم القائم but may not say
نعم الذي قام?

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
Al-Ḥasan read فلمّا ذاقا الشجرة بدت لهما سوأتهما, with the singular; the plural is better and the dual is permissible; we have discussed this in Sūrat al-Māʾida. وَطَفِقا: a sukūn on the fāʾ is also permissible.
Al-Akhfash reported طفق يطفق, like ضرب يضرب. Al-Ḥasan read يَخْصِفانِ with a kasra on the khāʾ [i.e. يِخِصِّفان]; the original form is يختصفان, which was assimilated, and the khāʾ given a kasra because two quiescent letters meet. Ibn Burayda and Yaʿqūb read يَخْصِفانِ ] with a fatḥa on the khāʾ [i.e. يَخَصِّفان], casting the vowel of the tāʾ onto it. [Translator's note: the printed vowelling of both variants repeats the main reading.] يخصّفان with a ḍamma on the yāʾ is also permissible, from خصّف يخصّف. The meaning is that they were made to abandon clothing, and their private parts became visible.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
قالا رَبَّنا: a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf); the original form is يا ربنا, and it has been said that [the omission of] «يا» carries the sense of reverence.
وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنا: (إن) is placed on (لم) because, together with what follows it, its meaning is that of a past verb.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: يا بَنِي آدَمَ: a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf). قَدْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكُمْ لِباساً يُوارِي سَوْآتِكُمْ: this is cotton and flax, because they come from water, which comes from the sky. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim in the transmission of al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī, and Abū ʿAmr in the transmission of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī read ورياشا. Abū ʿUbayd reported it only from al-Ḥasan and did not explain its meaning; it is the plural of ريش, which is what consists of wealth and clothing. Al-Farrāʾ said: ريش and رياش, as you say لبس and لباس. وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى: this is the reading of the people of Medina and al-Kisāʾī [Translator's note: their reading is ولباسَ, in the accusative; the printed vowelling shows the nominative in both places]; Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى in the nominative. The accusative is by conjunction, and the sentence is complete; the nominative is as a mubtadaʾ (subject). وذلِكَ is its naʿt (adjective), and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is خَيْرٌ. «لباس» may also be nominative on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "and covering the private parts — that is the clothing of the God-fearing". It is transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: the nominative and the accusative are both good, except that the accusative admits two meanings: one is that ذلك points to the clothing, and the other that it points to all that has preceded. As for لباس التقوى, there are two views on it. One is that the meaning of "He sent down the clothing of piety" is what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, taught and guided by — this in the accusative; and in the nominative by way of figurative representation. The other view is that the meaning of لباس التقوى is the wearing of wool and coarse garments by which one humbles oneself before Allah, Majestic and Mighty. The most fitting thing said about the accusative is that it is conjoined and «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, that is, "that which We have sent down of clothing and finery, the clothing of piety, is better than [your] piety and stripping naked in your circumambulation". If you use the nominative and read وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى, the most fitting thing said about it is that you make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with وذلِكَ as its naʿt, that is, "and the clothing of piety, that which you have come to know, is better for you than the clothing of garments that cover your private parts and than the finery We sent down to you; so put it on". ذلِكَ مِنْ آياتِ اللَّهِ, that is, of what indicates that he has a Creator. لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ, that is, so that they may be in hope of taking heed.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
يا بَنِي آدَمَ: a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf). لا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ: a prohibition; it is figurative, like وَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ [Āl ʿImrān: 102], that is, remain upon Islam until death comes to you. كَما: in the position of the accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar. أَخْرَجَ أَبَوَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ: أب, and أبة for the feminine; on this basis أبوان is said. In the vocative one says يا أبة for the masculine, with a ḍamma on the hāʾ and with a fatḥa.
يَنْزِعُ عَنْهُما لِباسَهُما: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also begin a new sentence. لِيُرِيَهُما: accusative by the lām. إِنَّهُ يَراكُمْ: the original form is يرأاكم, then the hamza was lightened. هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ: conjoined to the latent (mustatir) pronoun, and هو is emphasis (tawkīd). This indicates that رأيتك وعمر is ugly, and that the pronoun is not like the overt noun. It has been said:
His saying إِنَّهُ يَراكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا تَرَوْنَهُمْ indicates that the jinn are not seen except in the time of a prophet, so that this may be a proof of his prophethood, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, created them with a constitution in which they are not seen; they are seen only when they are transformed from their forms, and that is one of the miracles that occur only in the time of the prophets ﷺ. مِنْ حَيْثُ لا تَرَوْنَهُمْ: Sībawayh reported حيث [Translator's note: presumably with a different final vowel, e.g. حيثَ; the source does not mark it]. Abū Isḥāq said: it is indeclinable (mabnī) for two reasons: one is that it does not indicate a specific place, and the other is that what follows it is a ṣila (relative clause), because it is not put in construct. One also says حوث and حوث. The Kufans reported the kasra and the construct.
إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ أَوْلِياءَ لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ, that is, We have described them so.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: كَما بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, that is, "you will return as He began you", that is, as He created you the first time He will bring you back. Abū Isḥāq said: it is connected (mutaʿalliq) to what precedes it, that is, "and from it you will be brought forth; as He began you, you will return".

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
فَرِيقاً هَدى: accusative governed by هدى. وَفَرِيقاً: accusative by an implied verb, that is, "and He led a group astray". Sībawayh recited: [al-Munsariḥ] 146-
أصبحت لا أحمل السّلاح ولا ... أملك رأس البعير إن نّفرا
والذّئب أخشاه إن مررت به ... وحدي وأخشى الرّياح والمطرا
(I have become one who cannot carry weapons, nor control the camel's head if it bolts; and the wolf I fear if I pass it alone, and I fear the winds and the rain.)
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: the implied form is "they will return, a group guided and a group…", that is, they will return as two groups.
Al-Kisāʾī said: in the reading of Ubayy it is تعودون فريقين فريقا هدى وفريقا حقّ عليهم الضلالة. Al-Farrāʾ said: had it been nominative it would have been permissible. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read أنّهم with a fatḥa on the hamza, in the sense of "because they".

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: قُلْ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا خالِصَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), that is, "it is exclusively, on the Day of Resurrection, for those who believed in this world"; this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, and Nāfiʿ read it so. [Translator's note: the reading meant is خالصةٌ in the nominative; the printed vowelling shows the accusative.] The rest of the readers read خالِصَةً as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, it is due to them in this state, and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا. Sībawayh prefers the accusative because the adverbial phrase comes first. كَذلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
قُلْ إِنَّما حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ الْفَواحِشَ: accusative because the action of the verb falls on it. ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها وَما بَطَنَ: a badal (substitute).
وَالْإِثْمَ وَالْبَغْيَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ: al-Farrāʾ said: الإثم is what falls short of the ḥadd punishment, and البغي is overbearing conduct towards people. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for الإثم being wine, that is not known; the prohibition of wine is found explicitly in the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, namely His saying إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصابُ وَالْأَزْلامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطانِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ [al-Māʾida: 90]. The reality of الإثم is that it is all sins, as he said: [al-Kāmil] 147-
إنّي وجدت الأمر أرشده ... تقوى الإله، وشرّه الإثم
(I have found that the most rightly guided of affairs is fear of God, and the worst of it is sin.)
البغي is going beyond bounds in wrongdoing. وَأَنْ تُشْرِكُوا بِاللَّهِ: in the position of the accusative, conjoined, and likewise وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ; it makes clear that every polytheist says about Allah what he does not know.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ فَإِذا جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ, that is, the time known to Allah. لا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ ساعَةً: an adverb of time. وَلا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ: by this He indicated that the one who is killed is killed only at his appointed term.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: يا بَنِي آدَمَ إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ: a condition; the nūn entered for emphasis because of the entry of ما. فَمَنِ اتَّقى وَأَصْلَحَ: a condition, and what follows it is its apodosis (jawāb); it together with its apodosis is the apodosis of the first. [The meaning is] "and acted righteously among you". It has also been said: the meaning is "whoever is God-fearing and acts righteously, let him obey", and this was omitted. His saying, Majestic and Mighty, فَمَنِ اتَّقى وَأَصْلَحَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ indicates that the believers on the Day of Resurrection will neither fear nor grieve, and no terror or alarm will touch them.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها: a mubtadaʾ (subject). أُولئِكَ: a second mubtadaʾ. أَصْحابُ النَّارِ: the khabar (predicate) of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise أُولئِكَ يَنالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُمْ مِنَ الْكِتابِ, because the implied form is "attaining them" (نائل لهم). حَتَّى إِذا جاءَتْهُمْ: al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said about «حتّى», «أمّا» and «إلا» that they are not pronounced with imāla, because they are particles; so a distinction was made between them and nouns such as حبلى and سكرى. Abū Isḥāq said:
«حتى» is written with a yāʾ because it resembles سكرى; if «إلا» were written with a yāʾ it would resemble «إلى»; and «إما» is not written with a yāʾ because it is «إن» with «ما» joined to it.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: كُلَّما دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ: an adverb (ẓarf). حَتَّى إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا, that is, they gathered together. Al-Aʿmash read تداركوا, which is the original form; then assimilation occurred, so a connecting alif was needed. Mujāhid read حتى إذا أدركوا, that is, they overtook one another. جَمِيعاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). قالَ لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ وَلكِنْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ what you find of punishment.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: That is: you have disbelieved and done as we did, so you do not deserve any lightening of the punishment.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها: the noun of «إن», and the khabar (predicate) is in لا تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمْ أَبْوابُ السَّماءِ. This is the reading of Nāfiʿ. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read لا يفتح with the yāʾ [Translator's note: the source has "with the bāʾ", evidently a misprint for yāʾ], treating the plural as masculine; the feminine is on the feminine of the group. The light form is used for few and many, and the doubled form for many only; the doubled form is preferable here because it better indicates multiplicity.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: لَهُمْ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ مِهادٌ وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ غَواشٍ: the tanwīn, according to Sībawayh, is compensation for the yāʾ, and according to his followers compensation for the vowel. وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative because it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the khabar (predicate). The meaning of لا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَها is: except what it is able to do and has capacity for.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
وَنَزَعْنا ما فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ: if you need the plural of غلّ, you say غلال. تَجْرِي: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also begin a new sentence. وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدانا لِهذا: there are two views on it.
One is "He guided us to what led to this"; the other view is that the meaning is "who guided us to Paradise by enabling us and making it known [to us]". وَما كُنَّا لِنَهْتَدِيَ: the lām of negation (lām al-juḥūd). لَوْلا أَنْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ: «أن» is in the position of the nominative. وَنُودُوا أَنْ تِلْكُمُ الْجَنَّةُ: «أن» is in the position of the accusative, lightened from the heavy form; it may also be explicative of what they were called with, in which case it has no grammatical position. تِلْكُمُ الْجَنَّةُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: وَنادى أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ أَصْحابَ النَّارِ: [النار] is pronounced with imāla because of the rāʾ, since it is genitive and counts as two letters; tafkhīm (full pronunciation without imāla) is also permissible. أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنا: like «أن تلكم». فَهَلْ وَجَدْتُمْ ما وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمْ حَقًّا: two objects. قالُوا نَعَمْ: al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read قالُوا نَعَمْ with a kasra on the ʿayn [Translator's note: i.e. نَعِم; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading]; in this dialect a sukūn on the ʿayn is also permissible. فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ بَيْنَهُمْ أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ: this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Nāfiʿ. Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ ] [Translator's note: i.e. أنَّ لعنةَ; the printed vowelling repeats the first reading]. أَنْ is in the position of the accusative on both readings; with the lightened form it may also have no grammatical position and be explicative. Abū ʿUbayd reported that al-Aʿmash read أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ, and ʿIṣma reported from al-Aʿmash that he read أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ with a kasra on the hamza [i.e. إنّ]; this is on the basis of an implied verb of saying, as the Kufans read فناداه الملائكة وهو قائم يصلّي في المحراب إنّ الله.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الظالمين; the nominative and the accusative are also permissible, with something implied.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَبَيْنَهُما حِجابٌ: this is the wall that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, mentioned. وَعَلَى الْأَعْرافِ رِجالٌ, that is, on the elevations of the wall, which are its battlements; from it comes عرف الفرس (the horse's mane). The scholars have discussed the people of al-Aʿrāf. Some said: they are angels. It has also been said: they are people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal. Among the best that has been said about it is that the people of al-Aʿrāf are the just witnesses of the Resurrection, namely the witnesses from every nation who testify against people concerning their deeds; they are on the wall between Paradise and the Fire. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيماهُمْ وَنادَوْا أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ, that is, "you are safe from punishment". لَمْ يَدْخُلُوها وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ, that is, the people of al-Aʿrāf have not entered Paradise, that is, they have not entered it yet, وهم يطمعون — on this interpretation: and they know that they will enter it. It is well known in the language that طمع can mean "know".

nahhas-irab:200-200.t: وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نزغ: i.e. if Satan whispers to you, at the time of anger, something that is not lawful. فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ: [All-Hearing] of your saying; عَلِيمٌ: [All-Knowing] of what is required in that. يَنْزَغَنَّكَ is in the position of the jussive by the condition; it is emphasised with the nūn, and that is fitting when «ما» has entered. Sībawayh related: بألم ما تختننّه ("with pain you will be circumcised").

nahhas-irab:201-201.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا: i.e. they guarded against acts of disobedience. إِذا مَسَّهُمْ طائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ: this is the reading of the people of Basra and the people of Mecca; the people of Medina and the people of Kufa read طائفة; and it is related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr طيّف with a doubled yāʾ. [Translator's note: the attribution of readings here is as printed; in the standard transmission the people of Medina and Kufa read طائف and Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read طَيْف.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the speech of the Arabs in the like of this is طيف, lightened, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) from طاف يطيف; al-Kisāʾī said: it is lightened from طيّف. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of ṭayf in the language is what is imagined in the heart or seen in sleep, and likewise the meaning of ṭāʾif. Abū Ḥātim said: I asked al-Aṣmaʿī about طيّف and he said: among maṣdars there is no fayʿil. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not a maṣdar; rather it is in the sense of ṭāʾif. The meaning is: those who guard against acts of disobedience, when something from Satan reaches them, reflect on the power of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and on His favour to them, and so abandon the disobedience, and then they see clearly. It is related from Mujāhid تَذَكَّرُوا with a doubled dhāl [i.e. تَذَّكَّروا], and it has no construal in Arabic.

nahhas-irab:202-202.t: وَإِخْوانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الغَيِّ: Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar said: the pronoun is for the idolaters. Abū Ḥātim said: i.e. and the brothers of the idolaters, who are the devils. Abū Isḥāq said: there is fronting and postponement in the speech, the meaning being: "they cannot help them, nor can they help themselves, and their brothers draw them on in error". The best of what has been said on this is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk: وَإِخْوانُهُمْ, i.e. the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked. يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الغَيِّ ثُمَّ لا يُقْصِرُونَ: he said: i.e. they do not repent and do not turn back. On this view the pronoun is connected, and this is more fitting in Arabic. The wicked were called "brothers of the devils" because they accept from them. The people of Medina read يَمُدُّونَهُمْ with ḍamma on the yāʾ [i.e. يُمِدُّونهم], and a group of the philologists reject this reading, among them Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd. Abū Ḥātim said: I know no construal for it except that the meaning be "they increase them in error", and this is not what first comes to minds. A group of the philologists, among them Abū ʿUbayd, related that when a thing increases a thing by itself one says مدّه, and when it increases it by something else one says أمدّه, as in يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِخَمْسَةِ آلافٍ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ [Āl ʿImrān: 125]. It is related of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he argued for the reading of the people of Medina; he said: one says مددت له في كذا, i.e. I made it attractive to him and urged him to do it, and أمددته في كذا, i.e. I helped him with an opinion or the like. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read: وإخوانهم يمادّونهم في الغيّ.

nahhas-irab:203-203.t:
وَإِذا لَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بِآيَةٍ قالُوا لَوْلا: in the sense of «هلّا» ("why not"), and nothing follows it but a verb, overt or implied.
هذا بَصائِرُ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. this by which I have shown you that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is One.
بصائر: i.e. by which one gains insight. وَهُدىً: i.e. and guidance (indication). وَرَحْمَةٌ: i.e. and a blessing.

nahhas-irab:204-204.t: وَإِذا قُرِئَ الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned that it is said this concerns the prayers, and it was said that it concerns the sermon; linguistically it should apply to everything, unless some evidence indicates that something is specified.

nahhas-irab:205-205.t:
وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعاً وَخِيفَةً: a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The plural of خيفة is خوف, because it has the sense of الخوف; al-Farrāʾ related that one also says خيف. Abū Mijlaz read بالغدوّ والإيصال, and it is the maṣdar of آصلنا, i.e. we entered upon the evening. [Translator's note: the source prints «أصلنا».] وَالْآصالِ is the plural of أُصُل, like طُنُب and أطناب. Al-Akhfash said: الآصال is the plural of أصيل, like يمين and أيمان. Al-Farrāʾ said: أُصُل is the plural of أصيل, and أُصُل may be singular, as he said: [al-Basīṭ] 165-
ولا بأحسن منها إذ دنا الأصل
(Nor more beautiful than her when the late afternoon drew near.)

nahhas-irab:206-206.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ is the noun of «إنّ»; they are the angels, the blessings of Allah be upon them. Abū Isḥāq said: He said "with your Lord" — while Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is in every place — because they are near to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and everyone near to the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is "with Him". Another said: because they are in a place where nothing is executed except the judgement of Allah, Mighty and Exalted. And it was said: because they are the messengers of Allah, as one says: "With the caliph is a large army". وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ: i.e. they magnify Him and declare Him free of every evil. وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ: i.e. they humble themselves, unlike the people of disobedience.
